new_statements.quote: ...by giving as our main rule that the penultimate (the last syllable but one) is stressed, we get what would seem to most people the natural pronunciation of a very great many words ... To avoid such doubts it seems best to state the rule as in Idiom Neutral: stress the vowel preceding the last consonant. But this rule will have to be supplemented by the rule that the addition of the ordinary consonantal endings does not change the stress of the main word, thus we have stress on the first syllable of patros, patron, nulum, nulim, amad, and on the second of families, privatim, amusad—all in accordance with the principle of value.
new_statements.citation: Jespersen, Otto. 1928. An International Language. London: George Allen & Unwin. Part II 'Novial', section 'Stress', pp. 84-85.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Files checked under (1) Verbatim check: I viewed the full-resolution ONB page images and directly (not just the scanned). To avoid such doubts it seems best to state the rule as in Idiom Neutral: stress the vowel preceding the last consonant. But this rule will have to be supplemented by the rule that the addition of the ordinary consonantal endings does not change the stress of the main word,…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the syllable containing the last vowel that is followed by a consonant, computed on the word minus its inflectional consonant endings (-s plural, -n, -m accusative/neuter, -d past): i.e. final stress in consonant-final stems (privát, privátim), penultimate in words ending in a single vowel (formúle, Afríka, elefánte), and on the vowel before the consonant when the word ends in a vowel sequence (fúrie, Itália, famílie(s), galérie) — Jespersen chose this wording precisely so that it is indifferent to whether iV/uV counts as one or two syllables. Fully predictable, right-edge, no lexical accent marks; author frames it as essentially a penultimate rule.
new_statements.secondary_stress: p. 85: 'many derived words have a secondary rhythmic stress on the very syllable which some people would like to have seen stressed: fàsiléso, fòrmulísa, kònsulàl, amèrikáno, krìtikál, etc.' (rhythmic, separated from the main stress by one or two weak syllables, per p. 83).
new_statements.exceptions: Inflectional consonantal endings -s, -n, -m, -d are invisible to the rule (pátros, núlum, ámad; famílies, privátim, amúsad). Words with no consonant after the first vowel stress the first vowel (dúo, bóa). idée, héroo follow the rule though 'a little strange'. Jacob 1947 (p. ~86, citing Novialiste 18, 1937) reports a later amendment: words in -ee (kafée 'café' vs káfe 'coffee') stress the first e, i.e. -ee counts as one long stressed e.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level rule for citation/orthographic words of a constructed language (prescriptive design statement by the language's author); inflectional endings explicitly excluded from the computation; cf. also his remark 'Cf. below on adverbs' (-im adverbs keep stem stress).
new_statements.identity_note: Describes Novial as originally published by its author in 1928 (novi1234, ISO nov). Later revisions (1930 Lexike, 1934 orthographic reform, 1937 -ee amendment reported by Jacob 1947) do not change the basic placement rule. The rule is explicitly modelled on Idiom Neutral's.

To avoid such doubts it seems best to state the rule as in Idiom Neutral: stress the vowel preceding the last consonant. But this rule will have to be supplemented by the rule that the addition of the ordinary consonantal endings does not change the stress of the main word, thus we have stress on the first syllable of patros, patron, nulum, nulim, amad, and on the second of families, privatim, amusad—all in accordance with the principle of value.
sources.note: Main rule considered as penultimate stress, but restated to avoid syllabification doubts as: 'stress the vowel preceding the last consonant' (as in Idiom Neutral), supplemented by: the ordinary consonantal endings (-s, -n, -m, -d) do not change the stress of the main word (pátros, núlum, ámad; famílies, privátim, amúsad). Consequences spelled out: formúle, konsúle, Afríka, Ameríka; fúrie, Itália, Fránsia, galérie, enérgie; duo, boa stress first vowel; idée, héroo. sources.note: Second-hand restatement p. 73: 'The stress falls on the vowel preceding the last consonant. The addition of the ordinary consonant endings does not change the stress of the main word.' Also reports (Novialiste 18, 1937) that Jespersen later accepted that words in -ee (kafee 'cafe') stress the first e, an abrogation of the rule, with the flexional consonants -s, -d, -m, -n still excepted.
